questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: pick stored state for an account
questions.stem: A designer models a neighborhood savings account holding an owner name and a balance in cents. Which member belongs as stored state instead of behavior?

options.text: a deposit step that adds cents to the balance
a withdrawal step that removes cents from the balance
a printed statement line showing the balance

questions.explanation: Balance persists between calls so it is stored state; deposits, withdrawals, and printed lines are behavior or derived reports computed from that state.
questions.hint: Ask what the account must remember overnight.

questions.stem: A shelter models a rescue cat with a name, a weight in kilograms, and daily care routines. Which member belongs as behavior rather than stored state?

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.stem: A savings account offers withdraw(amount) that requires 0 < amount <= balance before running. What does that requirement state?

options.text: the precondition callers must meet before the call
the promise the method keeps after the call
the loop rule checked inside the method
the declared type of the balance field

questions.explanation: A precondition is the caller promise checked on entry; the exit promise is the postcondition, while types and loop rules play different roles.
questions.hint: Who must satisfy it, and when?

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.stem: A transit card value object stores a card number and a fare credit that must never change after the card is built. What makes the class immutable?

options.text: every field is set once in the builder and no method changes them
every field is public so anyone can rewrite it
a setter rewrites credit after each ride
the builder leaves fields unset until first use

questions.explanation: Immutability means state is fixed at build time with no mutators; public fields, setters, or deferred setup all permit later change.
questions.hint: When is the last legal change?

questions.stem: A pet shelter requires that a cat weight setter accept only values above zero and ignore the rest. What is the job of that setter guard?

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.stem: Trace this savings flow: class Vault { int balance; public Vault(int b) { balance = b; } public void deposit(int c) { balance += c; } public void withdraw(int c) { if (c > 0 && c <= balance) { balance -= c; } } } Vault v = new Vault(100); v.deposit(40); v.withdraw(30); System.out.print(v.balance); What prints?
questions.explanation: Deposit lifts 100 to 140 and the guarded withdrawal of 30 succeeds, leaving 110.
questions.hint: Apply the deposit first, then test the guard.

questions.stem: Trace this shelter cat: class Cat { int weight; public Cat(int w) { weight = w; } public void feed(int meal) { if (meal > 0) { weight += meal; } } public void play() { weight -= 1; } } Cat c = new Cat(6); c.feed(3); c.play(); System.out.print(c.weight); What prints?

questions.stem: Trace this transfer between savings accounts: class Till { int balance; public Till(int b) { balance = b; } public void moveTo(Till other, int c) { if (c > 0 && c <= balance) { balance -= c; other.balance += c; } } } Till a = new Till(80); Till b = new Till(20); a.moveTo(b, 50); System.out.print(a.balance + "-" + b.balance); What prints?
